comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory write-down impact on gross margin
comparisons.peer_summary: If assumptions regarding future demand or market conditions become less favorable, additional inventory write-downs may be required, negatively impacting gross margin; conversely, selling previously written-down inventory above its written-down value may result in a net benefit to gross margin.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose the specific impact of inventory write-downs on gross margin, including the counter-intuitive benefit of selling previously written-down inventory. MU reports that its 2024 gross margin was aided by 'lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023,' whereas AMD explicitly states as a general risk/policy that selling such inventory results in 'a net benefit to our gross margin' because revenue is recorded with 'a lower or no offsetting charge to cost of sales.'

sentences.text: Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).

If in any period we are able to sell inventories that had been written down to a level below the ultimate realized selling price in a previous period, related revenue would be recorded with a lower or no offsetting charge to cost of sales resulting in a net benefit to our gross margin in that period.

peer_results.rationale: While AVGO discusses gross margin changes driven by VMware amortization and product mix (avgo_2024_7_D049), it does not discuss inventory write-downs or the specific mechanics of inventory provisions affecting margin, which is the central topic of the MU disclosure. The other AVGO candidate (avgo_2024_7_D003) concerns fiscal year duration and is not comparable to the margin performance topic.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2024 Impairment and Depreciation Charges Impacting Gross Margin
comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin decreased by $4.4 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by $3.3 billion in impairment and accelerated depreciation charges related to manufacturing assets exceeding capacity for the Intel 7 process node, as well as $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC attribute significant changes in their consolidated gross margin to specific inventory-related or asset-impairment charges. INTC reports a $4.4 billion decrease in gross margin driven by 'higher 2024 impairment charges' and '$922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges.' Similarly, MU attributes its 2023 negative margin and 2024 recovery largely to 'charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023' and the subsequent cost benefits in 2024.

sentences.text: Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).
Our consolidated gross margin in 2024 decreased by $4.4 billion, or 20%, compared to 2023 due primarily to higher 2024 impairment charges and accelerated depreciation.

Our 2024 gross margin also decreased due to lower revenue, higher unit cost primarily from an increased mix of Intel 4 and Intel 7 products, higher period charges due to $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges recognized in 2024, and higher factory start-up costs.

comparisons.peer_summary: The net unfavorable impact on gross margin from inventory provisions and sales of previously written-down items was 2.7% in fiscal year 2024 and 7.5% in fiscal year 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies explicitly quantify the unfavorable gross margin impact caused by inventory provisions and the sale of previously written-down items. NVDA reports a specific 'unfavorable impact of 2.7% in fiscal year 2024' from these factors, while MU describes the mechanism driving its margin volatility, noting that its 2024 margin improvement came partly from 'lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023,' implying a similar dynamic of managing the residual financial effects of prior write-downs.

sentences.text: Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).
The net effect on our gross margin from inventory provisions and sales of items previously written down was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% in fiscal year 2024 and 7.5% in fiscal year 2023.

peer_results.rationale: QCOM's disclosures (qcom_2024_7_D011, qcom_2024_7_D024) state that gross margin percentages remained flat and do not provide details on inventory provisions, write-downs, or specific drivers of margin volatility comparable to MU's detailed explanation of ASPs and inventory costs.
